nodes.label: UK English house style
nodes.rationale: Site copy, commit messages, PR descriptions and docs must all use British spelling/grammar (-ise not -ize) so the whole body of work stays consistent — never drift to US spelling.

nodes.label: Constrained markdown editor buttons
nodes.rationale: The editor exposes only bold, italic, link, H2/H3, lists, quote and image, so editors can't produce layouts that fight the design.

nodes.label: Editable prose pages must be .md, never .mdx
nodes.rationale: MDX executes a literal < or { in prose as code; deeper pages were deliberately converted to .md so an editor can type anything without breaking the build.
nodes.norm_label: editable prose pages must be .md, never .mdx

nodes.label: site.ts as the model for editable/technical split
nodes.rationale: site.ts imports the editor-owned site.json then spreads developer-only technical constants last, so an editor can never override url/geo/mapEmbed/churchdeskOrgId; new settings should copy this pattern.
nodes.norm_label: site.ts as the model for editable/technical split

nodes.label: sitemap-meta.mjs reads lastmod from frontmatter, not file mtime
nodes.rationale: A CI checkout would otherwise date the whole archive to this morning if mtime were used.
nodes.norm_label: sitemap-meta.mjs reads lastmod from frontmatter, not file mtime

nodes.label: Children's Church age range default: 5–9
nodes.rationale: The live page itself states 5–9 in both heading and body, so 5–9 was used throughout despite the brief's nav/home mismatch.

nodes.label: Open item: .org vs .net email domain
nodes.rationale: A few live pages showed @barnabites.net; the site used .org throughout and flags confirmation of garden-team and vicar addresses.

nodes.label: Hero/MusicBand accessibility fix (sr-only description, not role=img)
nodes.rationale: role="img" would be an invalid nested-interactive container since the bands contain links, so a CSS background image plus a visually hidden .sr-only description is used instead.
nodes.norm_label: hero/musicband accessibility fix (sr-only description, not role=img)

nodes.label: Standardised Sung Mass duration wording
nodes.rationale: Three of the site's own sources disagreed (serviceTimes.json, VisitDetails.astro, Visiting page); none were ported from the live site, so standardised on 'about an hour and a quarter', the CMS-editable value two of three already agreed with.

nodes.label: Newsletter signup: consent-gated ChurchDesk widget loader
nodes.rationale: Implemented as the brief's 'robust' option (signup-loader.js, org 1901) with the public archive as an always-available fallback link, avoiding a fragile custom endpoint; functions/newsletter.ts was not created because the widget posts directly to ChurchDesk from the browser.
nodes.norm_label: newsletter signup: consent-gated churchdesk widget loader

nodes.label: Open item: safeguarding leads names
nodes.rationale: The live page names no safeguarding officers; the names on /safeguarding (Pat Chapman, Helen Ward, Angela Colman) come from the brief and must be verified with the parish.

nodes.label: Open item: Youth Group age range
nodes.rationale: Brief's home copy said '12 and up'; the live page says 10–16 and was treated as authoritative — confirm with parish.
nodes.norm_label: open item: youth group age range

nodes.label: Liturgical engine test-preservation rule
nodes.rationale: Add cases for any new feast and never weaken a test to make a change pass — the calendar must stay correct across years.

nodes.label: Liturgically alive design tenet
nodes.rationale: The hero artwork changes with the church season/feast, keyed off the liturgical engine; the footer shows a live season line.

nodes.label: Wiring the dormant hero/heroAlt page fields
nodes.rationale: pages schema already defines hero/heroAlt but they were not rendered or exposed in the CMS and no page set them; wiring is a no-op for existing pages and gives a free CMS photo slot.
nodes.norm_label: wiring the dormant hero/heroalt page fields

nodes.label: Decision: no migration to astro:assets, stay on public-path strings
nodes.rationale: CMS-uploaded images are referenced by public path and cannot be build-time imported, so the manual sharp → WebP convention is retained deliberately.
nodes.norm_label: decision: no migration to astro:assets, stay on public-path strings

nodes.label: Constraint: no hero added to the homepage
nodes.rationale: The existing top seasonal-artwork band stays; the photography rollout deliberately does not introduce a new photographic hero at the top of the homepage.
nodes.norm_label: constraint: no hero added to the homepage

nodes.label: Constraint: do not remove any current high-res image unless certain a new one is better
nodes.rationale: The only replacement candidates are the four seasonal hero artworks (procession, altar, worship, thurible), and only via an explicit per-image side-by-side review on parish approval.
nodes.norm_label: constraint: do not remove any current high-res image unless certain a new one is better

nodes.label: Safeguarding & consent publish gate for images of identifiable people
nodes.rationale: Several photos show identifiable individuals including children (youth group, choristers, Noisy Mass); implementation stages publishing such images must not merge until the parish confirms photo consent per its safeguarding policy.
nodes.norm_label: safeguarding & consent publish gate for images of identifiable people

nodes.label: fmt(label, value) music-typography rule (composer roman, title italic)
nodes.rationale: Replaces the old 'italicise everything after the first comma' rule, which broke on real entries (e.g. 'Riu, riu, chiu', 'Sumsion in G'); the new ordered rule strips trailing annotations, detects key suffixes, and only splits composer/title when the composer-shaped test passes.
nodes.norm_label: fmt(label, value) music-typography rule (composer roman, title italic)

nodes.label: Decision: group by calendar month, not liturgical season
nodes.rationale: These lists transfer feasts freely (e.g. Corpus Christi transferred to 30 May); the liturgy engine would confidently mislabel those with a season the parish isn't keeping — being subtly wrong is worse than plainly right, so the page groups by month as the printed lists do.
nodes.norm_label: decision: group by calendar month, not liturgical season

nodes.label: Picker fix: show earliest sheet dated between today and the coming Sunday inclusive
nodes.rationale: The old 14-day-window rule misfired on silent Sundays — e.g. on 26 December it would reach forward and show Epiphany's music a fortnight early on a Sunday meant to be blank. The precise rule delivers hide-on-silent-Sundays with no flag or marker files.
nodes.norm_label: picker fix: show earliest sheet dated between today and the coming sunday inclusive

nodes.label: Never invent parish facts principle
nodes.rationale: Where a fact is needed and unknown (fees, banns, names), build the structure and leave editable copy or a flagged slot rather than invent it.

nodes.label: Slug→component injection pattern
nodes.rationale: The Organ page injects a developer-owned OrganSpec component keyed off entry.id in [...slug].astro; Musicians and later VisitDetails/EnquireCTA reuse this precedent for dynamic, non-editable bits alongside editable prose.

nodes.label: YouTubeFacade privacy-first click-to-load rationale
nodes.rationale: Renders a self-hosted poster + accessible play button; the youtube-nocookie.com iframe is injected only on click, so no cookies or third-party requests load until the visitor opts in.

nodes.label: Classic-script ordering guarantees CMS global exists before registration call
nodes.rationale: Loading the Sveltia bundle as a classic script (not type=module) makes the global CMS available synchronously so registerPreviewStyle can be called right after, matching the canonical Decap pattern; fallback is to re-add editor.preview:false if it doesn't apply live.
nodes.norm_label: classic-script ordering guarantees cms global exists before registration call

nodes.label: No Sveltia source is forked — config + own files + documented JS API only
nodes.rationale: Keeps CMS upgrades safe — Sveltia is pinned at @sveltia/cms@0.165.1 and never patched.
nodes.norm_label: no sveltia source is forked — config + own files + documented js api only

nodes.label: Superpowers docs are historical records, not current instructions
nodes.rationale: Dated spec+plan pairs describe how a feature was designed and built at the time and may since have been superseded; current truth is always CLAUDE.md/AGENT-GUARDRAILS.md and the code itself.
nodes.norm_label: superpowers docs are historical records, not current instructions

nodes.label: Deploy reality: main is production, no staging
nodes.rationale: Merging to main triggers deploy.yml which builds and deploys to Cloudflare Pages within ~1 minute; a CMS Publish also commits to main, so the highest-consequence fact is never push directly to main — branch, PR, let CI go green.
nodes.norm_label: deploy reality: main is production, no staging

nodes.label: Go-live checklist (rotate credentials, re-own under church, attach domain)
nodes.rationale: Before the mockup becomes production: rotate shared GitHub OAuth secret + Cloudflare API token, move Cloudflare account/repo to church ownership, attach the real domain, and revert MOCKUP URLs in config.yml.
nodes.norm_label: go-live checklist (rotate credentials, re-own under church, attach domain)

nodes.label: Why a GitHub Action instead of native Cloudflare Git integration
nodes.rationale: The GitHub account was already linked to a different Cloudflare account, which blocked the native connector, so deploy.yml builds/deploys on every push to main instead.
nodes.norm_label: why a github action instead of native cloudflare git integration

nodes.label: Decision: Git-connected Pages project, not direct-upload
nodes.rationale: The mockup is the future production project; go-live is simply attaching the custom domain to the same project, and Publish commits to main writing realistic production behaviour.
nodes.norm_label: decision: git-connected pages project, not direct-upload

nodes.label: Implementation change: deploy.yml now also runs on a daily schedule
nodes.rationale: Because the site is static, new Date() is frozen at build time; without a nightly rebuild a fortnight without a CMS publish would leave the music list, This Sunday band, footer season line and What's On diary all naming a service already sung.
nodes.norm_label: implementation change: deploy.yml now also runs on a daily schedule

nodes.label: Decision: every event normalised to Europe/London civil date at ingest
nodes.rationale: Formatting a real instant in UTC — as the original getEvents() did — files a late-evening summer event on the wrong day and under the wrong month heading.
nodes.norm_label: decision: every event normalised to europe/london civil date at ingest

nodes.label: Decision: diary shows one row per repeating series
nodes.rationale: calendar.ics carries every occurrence; expanding a weekly event into the diary would bury the feasts.
nodes.norm_label: decision: diary shows one row per repeating series

nodes.label: Two-midnights all-day bug (fixed 3 August 2026)
nodes.rationale: node-ical parses DTSTART;VALUE=DATE at local midnight, not UTC midnight like the site's own date construction (civilFromDateOnly), silently losing a day on all-day feed events in any zone ahead of UTC (e.g. BST); fixed by routing feed dates through utcMidnightOfDateOnly. Invisible in UTC and zones behind UTC, so CI on ubuntu-latest stayed green while a maintainer's machine in BST failed — vitest.config.ts now pins the test timezone to Europe/London.

nodes.label: Dual-write invariant
nodes.rationale: A content collection's shape must be defined identically in the Zod schema (content.config.ts) and the CMS field list (config.yml); changing one without the other makes the editor and the build disagree.

nodes.label: The editability contract
nodes.rationale: Site must be run day-to-day by non-technical parish staff via Sveltia CMS at /admin; preserving and extending safe non-technical editing is a primary goal of every change, protected because it is the easiest thing to break without noticing.

nodes.label: Hidden legacySlug field
nodes.rationale: Protects ~129 news redirects from the old blog; must not be removed or dropped on save.

nodes.label: Local CMS editing via File System Access API (no proxy server)
nodes.rationale: Sveltia reads/writes files directly via the browser's File System Access API (Chrome/Edge), unlike Decap's local_backend/cms-proxy-server, so there is nothing extra to run.
nodes.norm_label: local cms editing via file system access api (no proxy server)

nodes.label: YAML anchor &pf shared field set for pages, with Worship as the exception
nodes.rationale: pages fields in config.yml are shared through &pf, but Worship spells its fields out separately (for the gallery), so a new page field must be added in both places or it will be missing on Worship.
nodes.norm_label: yaml anchor &pf shared field set for pages, with worship as the exception

nodes.label: Three typefaces, one job each
nodes.rationale: Montserrat for headings/nav/labels (700/600/500 weights), Cormorant Garamond decorative-only, Source Serif 4 for body copy; all self-hosted, no Google Fonts or web-font CDN.

nodes.label: .serif vs .title class distinction
nodes.rationale: .serif means Cormorant (decorative) and out-specifies the h1–h4 rule, silently reverting a heading if misapplied; non-heading title text should take .title instead.

nodes.label: Desktop nav breakpoint raised to 1180px
nodes.rationale: The primary nav bar was already close to overflowing at 1024px and the wider type scale narrows it further; 1180px matches --maxw so iPad landscape gets the full-screen mobile menu instead of a cramped single-line bar.

nodes.label: Homepage header now solid on every page
nodes.rationale: Previously the header floated transparently over the hero artwork leaving white nav type over whatever photo showed; the overlay prop was removed from Base.astro/SiteHeader.astro/index.astro in favour of hideBreadcrumbs, trading the hero starting below the header rather than at the very top.
nodes.norm_label: homepage header now solid on every page

nodes.label: Menu bar ran out of room — nav moved to its own band
nodes.rationale: Measured on the old single-row header at 1280px, the bar was at 100% capacity (1108px of 1109px available); the nav now sits on its own ruled band below the masthead, freeing ~218px of slack even with a 19-character label — important because nav.ts labels are editor-editable.
nodes.norm_label: menu bar ran out of room — nav moved to its own band

nodes.label: Typography change: a sans arrives (August 2026)
nodes.rationale: The site launched under a 'two serifs, no sans' rule, deliberately overturned: Montserrat now sets headings, titles, the menu bar and tracked uppercase labels, self-hosted like the others.

nodes.label: Responsive type scale in percentages, not px
nodes.rationale: The congregation skews elderly; root font-size steps up with viewport (103%/108%/111%) in percentages so a reader's own raised browser default is preserved, whereas a px value would silently override it. @media screen-scoped so print size still wins.
nodes.norm_label: responsive type scale in percentages, not px
